recipes.title: Traditional Ragù Bolognese with Garlic Bread

items.i: mixed beef, veal and pork mince
passata (tomato sauce), plus ½ bottle of water

steps: Cook the pancetta in a large pan over medium heat for 4–5 minutes until the fat renders and it's golden (no salt needed).
Add the onion, celery and carrot with a little salt and sauté 6–7 minutes, stirring, without letting them colour.
Turn the heat to medium-high, add the mince, let it sit a minute or two, then break it up and cook 8–10 minutes until no longer pink and the water has evaporated. Season.
Pour in the red wine and reduce by about 75%, 2–3 minutes, scraping up the browned bits.
Stir in the tomato paste, passata and the half bottle of water used to rinse it out. Bring to a simmer, check seasoning, then cook on low for at least 2 hours (up to 5). He cooked it 3.
Mix the butter, grated garlic, parsley, salt and pepper. Slice the bread almost all the way through, spread the butter between the slices, and bake 10–15 minutes while the pasta cooks.
About 20 minutes before the end, cook the pasta in salted water for 1 minute less than the packet says. Reserve some pasta water, then drain.
Stir the milk gently into the ragù over low heat. It balances the acidity and makes it creamy; don't let it boil or it can split.

Toss each serving of pasta in a pan with a couple of ladles of ragù and a splash of pasta water over higher heat. Add Parmesan, torn basil and pepper, then pile high with extra sauce and Parmesan on top.
recipes.notes: Amounts are from the video; the ragù freezes well, so make extra. No macros are given, so they're estimates per serving (with pasta, without garlic bread).
